refnamediv.refpurpose: set the user environment variables from a given UID

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: userenv-fromenv is a chain-loading utility that sets environment variables and then chain loads to next-prog with the execvp3 function.
next-prog may contain its own command‐line options, which userenv-fromenv will ignore.

userenv-fromenv takes the value given in the UID environment variable as a user ID to look up in the system account database. That variable can be set by commands such as getuidgid1, envuidgid1. or login-envuidgid1. It first looks up the account record whose name matches the value given in the LOGNAME environment variable, if that variable is set. If that account record's user ID field has the desired ID, it uses that record; otherwise, it looks up the account record by user ID.
refsection.note: This lookup by name falling back to lookup by ID allows for systems where multiple user names map to the same user ID in the system account database. It ensures that the right account record, with the desired name, home directory, and shell fields, is found and used.
refsection.para: From the contents of the account database record, it sets these environment variables.

refsection.title: User account database variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set unless the --no-set-user command‐line option is used:

listitem.para: Set to the pathname of the user's home directory, as given in the system account database, falling back if the field is blank to unset.
Set to the user's name, as given in the system account database, falling back if the field is blank to unset.

refsection.para: The following environment variables are set unless the --no-set-shell command‐line option is used:

listitem.para: Set to the pathname of the user's shell program, as given by the value of the shell capability in the login.conf5 database. There is a twofold default fallback if that capability is not set. The first default is the user's shell, as given in the system account database. If that field is blank, a further fallback is to the system's default B shell name that is hardwired into the C library. (This second fallback is in line with the behaviour of login1.)

refsection.title: Path variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set from the login.conf5 database if the --default-path command‐line option is used and they are not already set:

listitem.para: Set to the value of the path capability, defaulting if there is no capability to the system's default path that is hardwired into the C library.
Set to the value of the manpath capability, defaulting to unset if there is no capability.
Set to the value of the termpath capability, defaulting if there is no capability to /usr/local/etc/termcap:/etc/termcap:/usr/pkg/etc/termcap:/usr/share/misc/termcap.
Set to the value of the terminfopath capability, defaulting if there is no capability to /usr/local/etc/terminfo:/etc/terminfo:/usr/pkg/etc/terminfo:/usr/share/misc/terminfo.

refsection.title: Tools variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set from the login.conf5 database if the --default-tools command‐line option is used and they are not already set:

listitem.para: Set to the value of the editor capability, defaulting if there is no capability to ex. (POSIX gives two choices of universally available line editor. This is the one that is not ed1.)
Set to the value of the visual capability, defaulting if there is no capability to vi. (POSIX gives one choice of universally available full-screen editor.)

Set to the value of the pager capability, defaulting if there is no capability to more. If the --toolkit-pager command‐line option is used that default changes from the standard more1 to the console-tty37-viewer1 that comes in the same toolkit as userenv-fromenv.

Set to the value of the manpager capability, defaulting if there is no capability to more. If the --toolkit-pager command‐line option is used that default changes from the standard more1 to the console-tty37-viewer1 that comes in the same toolkit as userenv-fromenv, with its --discard-control-strings option. This environment variable is used by some man1 commands.

Set to the value of the manxmlviewer capability, defaulting if there is no capability to console-docbook-xml-viewer1 that comes in the same toolkit as userenv-fromenv. This environment variable is used by some man1 commands.

Set to the value of the wwwbrowser capability, defaulting if there is no capability to www-browser which is the name of the alternative from Debian's update-alternatives1 system. This environment variable is used by some man1 commands.

refsection.note: The default of more is the most portable choice. The Single Unix Specification dropped pg in 2017. less is not universal, and where it is available it is usually also available as more anyway. most is likewise not universal.

refsection.title: Terminal variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set from the login.conf5 database if the --default-term command‐line option is used and they are not already set:

listitem.para: Set to the value of the term capability, defaulting if there is no capability to ansi. The TERM variable will have been set for a login session by the TTY login system, and this default will thus not be required.

refsection.title: Locale variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set from the login.conf5 database if the --default-locale command‐line option is used and they are not already set:

listitem.para: Set to the value of the lang capability, defaulting to POSIX if there is no capability.
Set to the value of the charset capability, defaulting to UTF-8 if there is no capability.

refsection.title: Timezone variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set from the login.conf5 database if the --default-timezone command‐line option is used and they are not already set:

listitem.para: Set to the value of the timezone capability, defaulting to UTC if there is no capability.

refsection.title: XDG variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set if the --set-xdg command‐line option is used:

listitem.para: Set to /run/user/username/.

variablelist.varlistentry:
XDG_CONFIG_DIRS
Set to /usr/local/etc/xdg:/etc/xdg:/usr/pkg/etc/xdg. The addition of /usr/local/etc comes from the BSDs. /usr/pkg/etc is the conventional $LOCALBASE/etc from NetBSD pkgsrc.

listitem.para: Unset, so that applications use the default of $HOME/.config.
Set to /usr/local/share:/usr/pkg/share:/usr/share:/share. The addition of /share comes from TrueOS Desktop. /usr/pkg/share is the conventional $LOCALBASE/share from NetBSD pkgsrc.
listitem.note: TrueOS Desktop ordered the directories the other way around, giving operating system data files priority over site local ones. This ordering, on the other hand, is the ordering that is used in the XDG Desktop Specification.

listitem.para: Unset, so that applications use the default of $HOME/.local/share.
Unset, so that applications use the default of $HOME/.local/state.
Unset, so that applications use the default of $HOME/.cache.
The value $HOME/.local/bin is prepended, after any login.conf5 processing has been done.
The value $HOME/.local/share/man is prepended, after any login.conf5 processing has been done.
The value $HOME/.config/termcap is prepended, after any login.conf5 processing has been done.

refsection.title: Desktop Bus variables
refsection.para: The following environment variables are set if the --set-dbus command‐line option is used:

listitem.para: Set to unix:path=/run/user/username/bus. (In practice, unix:runtime=yes is not actually supported yet by most operating systems.)

refsection.title: Other variables
refsection.para: If the --set-other command‐line option is used, all environment variables are set from the setenv capability in the login.conf5 database. Both the system and user databases are processed. In line with the behaviour of login1, any conflicting environment variables set here will be overridden by the variables taken from other capabilities and from the user account database, with the exceptions of the tools, XDG, and Desktop Bus variables, which will conversely be overriden by any settings here. This ordering is because the tools, XDG, and Desktop Bus variables are an extension, setting variables for which people will have been using setenv.

refsection.title: bugs and compatibility
refsection.para: As of version 1.34 this program no longer employs the GNU C library nor the BSD C library for environment variable handling. The previously documented workaround for those libraries' having memory leaks in their setenv3 and clearenv3 functions, is therefore no longer necessary.

The FreeBSD login_getpath3 library function has a bug that makes it impossible to specify paths containing space characters. This command implements the OpenBSD mechanism of allowing space characters, in the path and manpath capabilities, to be escaped with a backslash.

The FreeBSD login_getcaplist3 library function has several bugs, one of which makes it impossible to specify paths containing comma characters. This command implements the OpenBSD mechanism of allowing comma characters, in the setenv capability, to be escaped with a backslash.

In both cases, the backslash must be itself escaped again in the actual capability file text, as this is two levels of escaping. First the comma/space is escaped to make an escape sequence in the unencoded capability string, then the capability string is encoded with a second level of escaping in order to store it as text in the capability file.

Unlike the OpenBSD behaviour, this command does not restrict the expansion of ~ and $ to certain places in the aforementioned environment list and path strings. To include literal tildes and dollar characters anywhere in environment lists and paths, those characters too must always be (double) escaped with a backslash.
